import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

**Task:** call your app's methods from a frontend or a script with types checked
by the compiler, and find out before publishing whether a new version breaks
the clients already out there.

Every app embeds its [ABI](/core/build/app-abi/): its methods, their parameters
and results, its errors and events. `mero-app-build codegen` turns it into an
OpenAPI 3.1 document and a thin typed client over the client you already use:
mero-js's `CalimeroClient` (its `client.apps.call` and `client.apps.view`),
calimero-client-py's `Client` (the same, answering JSON), or the `CalimeroClient`
and `ContextContractCalling` of swift-sdk (MeroKit) and kotlin-sdk (mero-core). They keep doing the
work (the attested, sealed channel, sessions, passkey step-ups, retries); the
generated code only adds the method names and types.

## Generate a client

Put `mero-app-build` on PATH once, build the app, then point `codegen` at the
component, the `.mpk` bundle or an ABI JSON file (`meroctl context abi` saves an
installed app's). Every release ships it prebuilt for Linux (x86_64, aarch64) and
macOS (aarch64), named `mero-app-build_<target>.tar.gz` and listed in the
release's `SHA256SUMS`, so CI that only runs `codegen` needs no Rust toolchain;
from a core checkout, `scripts/install-mero-app-build.sh` builds it instead.
`mero-app-build --version` names the release it came from.

```bash
V=<release> T=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu   # the core release, and this machine's target
curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/calimero-network/core/releases/download/$V/mero-app-build_$T.tar.gz"
curl -fsSL "https://github.com/calimero-network/core/releases/download/$V/SHA256SUMS" \
  | grep " mero-app-build_$T.tar.gz\$" | sha256sum -c
tar -xzf "mero-app-build_$T.tar.gz" -C ~/.local/bin mero-app-build
```


```bash
mero-app-build apps/kv-store --out kv-store.wasm
mero-app-build codegen --abi kv-store.wasm --lang ts -o src/generated
```

```
wrote src/generated/openapi.json
wrote src/generated/client.ts
```

`--lang` is `ts`, `python`, `swift`, `kotlin` or `openapi` (the document alone).
Every language writes `openapi.json` beside the client (`client.ts`, `client.py`,
`KvStoreClient.swift`, `KvStoreClient.kt`) unless `--no-openapi` says not to.
The ABI carries no app name, so the client class is named after `--name`, else
the package of an `.mpk`, else the file's name (`kv-store.wasm` gives
`KvStoreClient`). A file named for what it holds (`abi.json`,
`app.component.wasm`) names no app: the class is then named after the crate whose
`Cargo.toml` is nearest above the file (`logic/res/abi.json` beside
`logic/Cargo.toml`'s `name = "kv-store"`), and with no such crate `codegen` stops
and asks for `--name`. A Kotlin client goes in `--package` (default
`calimero.generated.<name>`, here `calimero.generated.kvstore`). A multi-service
bundle writes one directory per service, each Kotlin client in `<package>.<service>`;
`--service <name>` picks one. Pass `--kotlin-serialization-plugin` when the Kotlin
module that compiles the client applies the kotlinx.serialization compiler plugin
(below). `mero-app-build --version` prints the release and the source it was built
from (`1.0.0-rc.19 (1.0.0-rc.19-11-g3da5b6edb, 3da5b6edb)`); `--help` prints the usage.

## Use it from TypeScript

```ts
import { CalimeroClient, passkeyConfirm } from '@calimero-network/mero-js';
import { KvStoreClient } from './generated/client';

const client = /* a signed-in CalimeroClient */;
const kv = new KvStoreClient(client, appId);

await kv.set({ key: 'greeting', value: 'hello' });
const value: string | null = await kv.get({ key: 'greeting' });
const count: string = await kv.len(); // u64: a decimal string

for await (const event of kv.events()) {
  if (event.kind === 'Inserted') console.log(event.data.key, event.data.value);
}
```

A call takes `{ idempotencyKey, confirm, signal }` as its last argument, a view
`{ consistency, minIndex, signal }` (`consistency: 'stale'` reads the replica that
answers). A `confirm` method's `412 CONFIRM_REQUIRED` step-up is answered by the
call's `confirm`, else by the `confirm` the `CalimeroClient` was built with
(here `rooms` is `apps/rooms`' generated client):

```ts
await rooms.adminRelease({ id, reason }, { confirm: passkeyConfirm(passkey) });
```

An `option<..>` argument may be left out or be `null`: the SDK reads both as
`None`. Every generated client leaves out an optional argument the caller does
not set: TypeScript sends the `args` object as given (a key left out stays out),
and the Python, Swift and Kotlin methods leave out a `None` / `nil` / `null`
argument rather than sending `null`. In an error's or an event's fields it is
always there, `null` for none.

### Read a call's log index and events

Each method answers its result alone. The same methods under `raw` answer the
whole answer: a call `{ result, index, events }` (`CallAnswer<T>`: the log index
it committed at and the app's events it emitted, typed as `AppEvent`), a view
`{ result, index }` (`ViewAnswer<T>`: the log index of the state it read). Use
them to resume the event stream from what a call or view already reflects, or to
read a later view at least as new as a call:

```ts
const { index, events } = await kv.raw.set({ key: 'greeting', value: 'hello' });
const value = await kv.get({ key: 'greeting' }, { consistency: 'stale', minIndex: index });

// Render the entries, then follow the events after the state they reflect.
const { result: entries, index: seen } = await kv.raw.entries();
for await (const event of kv.events(seen + 1)) { /* ... */ }
```

`raw` takes the same arguments and options, and runs `after` the same way. Its
type is `<Name>RawApi` (`KvStoreRawApi`). If the app has a method named `raw`,
the property is `rawAnswers`.

### Create an instance with its `init` arguments

When the app's `#[app::init]` takes arguments (here mero-chess's
`init(title: Option<String>, now: Option<u64>)`), the client declares them as
`InitArgs`, in the types of every other argument (a `u64` is a decimal string, an
`option` may be left out). `client.apps.create` takes `initArgs` as any JSON, so
check it with `satisfies`:

```ts
import type { InitArgs } from './generated/client';

const { appId } = await client.apps.create({
  package: 'com.calimero.mero-chess',
  initArgs: { title: 'Friday blitz', now: String(Date.now()) } satisfies InitArgs,
});
```

An `init` without arguments declares no `InitArgs`.

### Keep a refreshed session

mero-js refreshes an expired session on its own, and has no event that says it
did. A page that stores the session passes `after`, which runs after every call
and view, refused ones included:

```ts
const kv = new KvStoreClient(client, appId, {
  after: () => saveSession(client.session),
});
```

### Test without a node

The class implements `KvStoreApi` (`<Name>Api`), an interface of the app's
methods alone. Code that takes a `KvStoreApi`, or the `Pick` of it that it calls,
is handed the class in the app and a double of those methods in a test; there
is no need to `Pick` from the class itself (`Pick<KvStoreClient, 'len'>`).
Code that reads `raw` takes `KvStoreRawApi` the same way (`kv.raw` in the app):

```tsx
import type { KvStoreApi, KvStoreRawApi } from './generated/client';

function Counter({ kv }: { kv: Pick<KvStoreApi, 'len'> }) { /* ... */ }

render(<Counter kv={{ len: async () => '3' }} />);

async function save(kv: Pick<KvStoreRawApi, 'set'>): Promise<number> {
  return (await kv.set({ key: 'a', value: 'b' })).index;
}

await save({ set: async () => ({ result: null, index: 7, events: [] }) });
```

To test the class itself, give it a double of the part of `CalimeroClient` it
uses. A client that only calls and views takes an `AppCallTransport`
(`apps.call` and `apps.view`; `Pick<CalimeroClient, 'apps'>` is one), and has no
`events()`: calling it does not type-check. `events()` needs an `AppTransport`,
which adds `events`:

```ts
const kv = new KvStoreClient(
  {
    apps: {
      call: async () => ({ result: null }),
      view: async ({ method }) => ({ result: method === 'len' ? '0' : null }),
    },
  },
  'app-1',
);
```

A double may answer `{ result }` alone; it answers `raw` with index `0` and no
events unless it also gives `index` (and a call's `events`), as mero-js does.
`KvStoreClient` written without a type argument is a client with events
(`KvStoreClient<AppTransport>`), which is what one built on a `CalimeroClient` is.

## Use it from Python

```python
from calimero import Client
from generated.client import KvStoreClient

kv = KvStoreClient(client, app_id)  # a signed-in calimero Client
kv.set("greeting", "hello")
assert kv.get("greeting") == "hello"
assert kv.len(consistency="stale") == "1"
rooms.admin_release("b-1", "late", passkey=passkey)  # apps/rooms' confirm method
```

Arguments are keyword arguments in snake_case (`room_id=`); errors and events
are `TypedDict`s (`NotFoundError`, `InsertedEvent`). A call also takes
`idempotency_key=`, a `confirm` method `passkey=` (else the client's own), and a
view `consistency=` and `min_index=`.

## Use it from Swift

The client is a `Sendable` struct over swift-sdk's MeroKit, 2.0 or later (`import MeroKit`):

```swift
import MeroKit

// Every method: idempotency keys, stale views, `confirm` step-ups, events.
let kv = KvStoreClient(client: calimeroClient, app: appId)
// Or the contract an app already holds (MeroAppSession's backend, a test double):
let kv = KvStoreClient(backend: session.backend!, app: appId)

try await kv.set(key: "greeting", value: "hello")
let value: String? = try await kv.get(key: "greeting")
let count: UInt64 = try await kv.len()  // u64: a decimal string on the wire

for try await frame in kv.events() {
    if case .inserted(let key, let value) = frame.event { print(key, value) }
}

do {
    try await kv.remove(key: "missing")
} catch let error as AppError {
    if case .notFound = KvStoreClient.Refusal(error) { /* ... */ }
}
```

A call takes `idempotencyKey:` last, a view `stale:` and `minIndex:`, a `confirm`
method `passkey:`. Over a `ContextContractCalling` (`init(contract:)`,
`init(backend:app:)`) a view is `query` and a call `execute`; `confirm` methods,
`events()` and an `idempotencyKey` need `init(client:app:)` and throw
`MeroAppBackendUnsupported` otherwise. Decode `MeroAppBackend.events` with
`KvStoreClient.Event(kind:data:)`. Put each client in a module of its own (one
target per service).

## Use it from Kotlin

The client class is over kotlin-sdk's mero-core, 2.0 or later, with kotlinx.serialization
and kotlinx.coroutines on the classpath (no serialization plugin needed):

```kotlin
val kv = KvStoreClient(calimeroClient, appId)        // every method
val kv = KvStoreClient(backend, appId)               // MeroAppBackend's contract

kv.set(key = "greeting", value = "hello")
val value: String? = kv.get(key = "greeting")
val count: ULong = kv.len()

kv.events().collect { frame ->
    when (val event = frame.event) {
        is KvStoreClient.Event.Inserted -> println("${event.key} ${event.value}")
        else -> {}
    }
}

try {
    kv.remove(key = "missing")
} catch (e: AppError) {
    if (KvStoreClient.Refusal.from(e) is KvStoreClient.Refusal.NotFound) { /* ... */ }
}
```

The trailing parameters and the two ways to build it are Swift's:
`(client, app)` runs every method; `(contract)` and `(backend, app)` run calls and
views and throw `UnsupportedOperationException` for the rest. Decode
`MeroAppBackend.events` with `KvStoreClient.Event.decode(kind, data)`.

## How the types come out

In TypeScript and Python `u64` and `i64` are decimal strings and `bytes` base64url
strings, as on the wire; Swift and Kotlin take and give `UInt64`/`ULong`,
`Int64`/`Long` and `Data`/`ByteArray` and write the wire forms themselves.
`u64_number` / `i64_number` (a `#[abi(plain)]` field) are JSON numbers: `number` in
TypeScript (exact only up to 2^53), `int` in Python, and the same `UInt64`/`ULong`,
`Int64`/`Long` written as numbers; `byte_list` is `number[]`, `List[int]`,
`[UInt8]`, `List<UByte>`. `option<T>` is `T | null` (`Optional[T]`, `T?`) and an
optional argument may be left out (every client leaves out one that is not set). Errors and events are typed:
`NotFoundError` / `InsertedEvent` in TypeScript and Python, the cases of
`Refusal` and `Event` in Swift and Kotlin. The full table is in
[App interface](/core/build/app-abi/#types).

Your own types come from the ABI's `types`: a record is an interface (a
`TypedDict`), an enum a union of its variants as serde writes them (`'Open'`,
`{ Closed: { at: string } }`, `{ type: 'published'; at: string }`), and a generic
type stays generic in TypeScript (`Listing<Slot>`) and is instantiated in Python
(`Listing_Slot`).

In Swift and Kotlin they are types nested in the client (`KvStoreClient.Slot`),
whose coding writes the same JSON:

| ABI shape | Swift | Kotlin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| record | `struct` with a `var` per field, `Codable, Sendable, Equatable` | `data class`, its serializer `Slot.serializer()` |
| newtype / `transparent` | `struct` with `value` | `data class` with `value` |
| tuple struct / unit struct | `struct` with `v0`, `v1`, ... / with nothing (`null`) | `data class` with `v0`, `v1`, ... / `data object` |
| enum | `enum`, a case per variant (`.closed(at:)`, `.moved(_:)`) | `sealed interface`, a `data class` or `data object` per variant |
| generic (`Listing<T>`) | generic (`Listing<Slot>`) | generic (`Listing.serializer(Slot.serializer())`) |

Each enum reads and writes the tagging serde gives it: externally tagged as
`"Open"` or `{ "Closed": { .. } }` (`{ "Open": null }` is read too), internally
tagged as the variant's fields beside its `tag` (a newtype variant's own object),
adjacently tagged as `{ tag, content }` (a unit variant without `content`), and
untagged as the data alone, trying the variants in order as serde does. Unknown
variant names and arrays of the wrong length are refused. A type that holds itself
works: a Swift enum that does is `indirect`, and a Swift field that holds its own
type outside an array or a dictionary (`option<Tree>`) is stored boxed
(`@Indirect`); Kotlin needs nothing. Fields the JSON may leave out are optional
(`nil` / `null`; Python's `TypedDict` puts them in a `total=False` part, so a caller
may leave them out) and left out when unset; any other `option` is written as
`null`. Kotlin's serializers are written out in the client, so no serialization
plugin is needed: pass them where kotlinx.serialization takes one. Each type is
also annotated `@Serializable(with = ...)` naming its serializer, so
`serializer<Slot>()` finds it, sealed interfaces too: by reflection on the
companion's `serializer()`, which kotlinx's bundled R8 rules keep for
`@Serializable` classes. A module that applies the kotlinx.serialization compiler
plugin generates with `--kotlin-serialization-plugin`: the plugin then writes each
`serializer()` itself (a hand-written one would clash with it, "Overload resolution
ambiguity") and resolves `serializer<T>()` without reflection; call sites
(`Slot.serializer()`) stay the same.

<Aside type="caution">
  A type is described when it derives `Record` or `AbiType`
  ([SDK macros](/core/build/sdk-macros/#deriveabitype)). Any other type, and every
  type of an app built before the SDK wrote `types`, is `unknown` (`Any`): cast or
  validate the value where you use it, or rebuild the app. The Swift and Kotlin
  clients type it MeroKit's `JSONValue` / kotlinx's `JsonElement` (Swift under a
  nested alias with the type's name; Kotlin as `JsonElement` itself, since a
  top-level alias would clash with an app type of that name in the package): decode
  it where you use it.
</Aside>

## Use any OpenAPI tool

`openapi.json` is a standard OpenAPI 3.1 document: each method is
`POST /apps/{app}/methods/{name}`, and its body is `{ args, idempotencyKey? }` for a
call or `{ args, consistency?, minIndex? }` for a view. A running node serves the
same document for an installed app at `GET /apps/{app}/openapi.json`. Generators
and validators read it as they read any other; give the generated code mero-js
or calimero-client-py as its transport, since the node answers only inside the
sealed channel.

## Check a new version before publishing

Compare the new build with the last release:

```bash
mero-app-build abi-diff dist/kv-store-1.0.0.mpk kv-store.wasm
```

```
breaking   method get: result changed: option<string> -> string
compatible method count: added (view)
```

It exits `1` when a change breaks existing callers, so it can gate CI. The rules
are in [App interface](/core/build/app-abi/#check-a-new-version-against-the-last).
Signing runs the same check when you name the last release:

```bash
mero-sign sign manifest.json --key release.key --previous dist/kv-store-1.0.0.mpk
python3 -I scripts/pack-component.py --wasm kv-store.wasm --package com.example.kv-store \
  --app-version 1.1.0 --previous dist/kv-store-1.0.0.mpk --out dist/kv-store-1.1.0.mpk
```

Breaking changes are printed as a warning. A state field removed or changed in
kind while the state version stayed the same is refused: bump
`#[app::state(version = N)]` and migrate the data
([Upgrades & state](/core/build/migrations/)).
